text.tutorial.welcome: Welcome to Punto Banco. Two hands are dealt every coup: the Player (Punto) and the Banker (Banco). The hand closer to 9 wins. Nobody makes decisions. Every draw is fixed by the rules, and as the dealer your job is to apply them quickly and without mistakes. This short tutorial takes about five minutes. You can skip it at any time and reopen it from the menu.
text.tutorial.values: Card values. Ace counts 1. Cards 2 to 9 count their face value. 10, Jack, Queen and King count 0. A hand is worth only the last digit of its total. 7 + 8 = 15, so the hand is 5. 9 + 9 = 18, so the hand is 8.
text.tutorial.deal: Dealing the first four cards. Deal four cards face up: Player, Banker, Player, Banker. Then call the Player first and the Banker second, for example "Player has nine, Banker has five." Watch the app deal one coup.
text.tutorial.natural: Step 1: Naturals. If either hand has 8 or 9 on its first two cards, that is a natural. Nobody draws. Call the result straight away. Here the Player would normally draw on 0, but the Banker has a natural 8, so the coup is over. Try it yourself.
text.tutorial.player-draws: Step 2: The Player rule. Player on 0 to 5 draws one card. Player on 6 or 7 stands. Call the card before you draw it: "One card to the Player." Here the Player has 5, so the Player draws.
text.tutorial.player-stands: Player stands on 6 or 7. Here the Player has 6 and stands. The Banker has 7 and also stands. Try dealing it.
text.tutorial.bank-stood: Step 3a: Banker when the Player stood. If the Player stood with two cards, the Banker looks only at its own hand, exactly like the Player: draws on 0 to 5, stands on 6 or 7. Here the Player stands on 7 and the Banker has 5, so the Banker draws.
text.tutorial.bank-drew: Step 3b: Banker when the Player drew. Now the Banker looks at its own total and the value of the Player's third card. Banker 0, 1 or 2: always draws. Banker 3: draws, unless the Player's third card is an 8. Banker 4: draws if the third card is 2 to 7. Banker 5: draws if the third card is 4 to 7. Banker 6: draws only if the third card is 6 or 7. Banker 7: always stands. Here the Banker has 3 and the Player's third card is an 8, so the Banker stands.
text.tutorial.bank-try-4: Your turn: Banker 4. The Banker has 4. Check the Player's third card against the rule: 4 draws on 2 to 7.
text.tutorial.bank-try-6: Your turn: Banker 6. The Banker has 6. It draws only against a Player third card of 6 or 7.
text.tutorial.three-card-8: A three-card 8 is not a natural. Only the first two cards can make a natural. If the Player draws to 8, the Banker still follows the rules.
text.tutorial.egalite: Result and Égalité. The hand closer to 9 wins. Call it, for example: "Banker wins, seven over six." Equal totals are Égalité: call "Égalité, eight each." Player and Banker bets stand off (neither wins nor loses), and Égalité bets pay 9 to 1. In this example both hands have a natural 8. Pay all winning bets before you pick up any cards.
text.tutorial.pickup: Clearing the table. Pay all winning bets first. Only then clear the cards (Rank 8.12 v). Tap the shuffler or Clear table, and all the cards go back into the continuous shuffler together.
text.tutorial.payouts: Payouts. Player wins pay even money: £20 wins £20. Banker wins pay 19 to 20. The house takes 5% commission, called the tax: £20 wins £19. Égalité pays 9 to 1: £10 wins £90.
text.tutorial.tax-maths: Working out the 5% tax. Quick way: take 10% and halve it. £340: 10% is £34, half is £17. Or count £1 for every £20 staked. £260 is 13 twenties, so £13 tax. Banco bets go up in £5 steps, because the smallest chip is 25p and the tax has to come out in whole chips.
text.tutorial.tax-money: When customers hand you money. Exact tax: on a £100 win the customer gives £5. Pay the full £100 and say "One hundred paid, five tax received." Change: on a £50 win the customer gives a £5 chip for a £2.50 tax. Pay £50 and give £2.50 change. Nothing given: take the tax from the winnings. On £200, pay £190. Making it even: on a £30 win the net would be £28.50. If the customer adds 50p, pay £29. Always announce the amount paid and the tax taken or received.
text.tutorial.done: You're ready. Practice deals endless coups from a continuous shuffler. Scenarios drill one rule at a time. Rules has the full sheet and the commission calculator. Use Hint whenever you are stuck. Your stats are saved on this device.
text.SHOE_FINISHED.1: The shoe is finished. Start a new shoe.
text.LAST_COUP_NOT_DUE.1: A continuous shuffler has no cut card and no last coup.
text.LAST_COUP_NOT_DUE.2: The cut card has not come out, so this is not the last coup.
text.LAST_COUP_NOT_ANNOUNCED.1: The cut card is out. Announce 'Last coup of this shoe' first.
text.BURN_NOT_DUE.1: The burn is done once, before the first coup.
text.BURN_REQUIRED.1: Burn one card from the shoe before the first coup.
text.CARD_ALREADY_IN_HAND.1: Place the card you are holding before drawing another.
text.CALL_TOTALS_FIRST.1: Announce both totals before any third card, e.g. 'Player has two, Banker has five'.
text.THIRD_CARD_NOT_CALLED.1: Call the third card before drawing it, e.g. 'One card to the Player'.
text.ILLEGAL_THIRD_CARD.1: No more cards are due on this coup. Call the result.
text.NOT_ALLOWED_NOW.1: You cannot draw a card now. Finish this coup first.
text.NO_CARD_IN_HAND.1: Draw a card from the shoe first.
text.WRONG_BOX.1: This card goes to the Player.
text.WRONG_BOX.2: This card goes to the Banker.
text.WRONG_BOX.3: You called a card to the Player; it goes there.
text.WRONG_BOX.4: You called a card to the Banker; it goes there.
text.TOTALS_NOT_DUE.1: Totals are called once all four initial cards are down.
text.THIRD_CARD_ALREADY_CALLED.1: You've already called a card to the Player. Draw it and place it.
text.THIRD_CARD_ALREADY_CALLED.2: You've already called a card to the Banker. Draw it and place it.
text.UNDER_DRAW.1: A third card is still due. Check the tableau.
text.RESULT_NOT_DUE.1: The result is called once the coup is complete.
text.PICKUP_BEFORE_PAYOUTS.1: Leave the cards down until all winning bets are paid.
text.NOT_ALLOWED_NOW.2: Cards are picked up only after the result and payouts.
text.NOT_ALLOWED_NOW.3: That card is not on the table.
text.WRONG_PICKUP_ORDER.1: Pick up the Player's first two cards, then the Banker's two, then the Player's third, then the Banker's third.
text.DISCARD_NOT_DUE.1: The table is cleared once the result is called and payouts are done.
text.DISCARD_NOT_DUE.2: Pick up every card in order before discarding.
text.ILLEGAL_THIRD_CARD.2: The next card goes to the Player, not the Banker.
text.ILLEGAL_THIRD_CARD.3: The next card goes to the Banker, not the Player.
text.ILLEGAL_THIRD_CARD.4: The Player does not take a third card here.
text.ILLEGAL_THIRD_CARD.5: The Banker does not take a third card here.
text.scenario.nat-p9: A two-card 9 is a natural. No third card to either hand.
text.scenario.nat-b8-vs-p0: Player on 0 would normally draw, but the Banker natural stops all draws.
text.scenario.nat-9-over-8: Both hands natural: compare totals, no draws.
text.scenario.nat-tie: Both hands 8: Égalité. Player and Banker bets stand off.
text.scenario.three-card-8: Player draws to 8, but it is not a natural; the Bank on 7 still stands by the tableau and loses 8 to 7.
text.scenario.p5-draws: Player draws on 0 to 5. 5 is the highest total that draws.
text.scenario.court-zeroes: Tens and court cards count zero: both hands 0, Player draws, then Bank 0 draws.
text.scenario.stood-b5-draws: When the Player stands, the Bank regards only its own hand and draws on 0 to 5.
text.scenario.stood-b6-stands: Bank 6 only draws against a Player third card of 6 or 7. With no Player third card, it stands.
text.scenario.b2-vs-9: Bank on 0 to 2 always draws once the Player has drawn.
text.scenario.b3-vs-8: Bank 3 draws against everything except a Player third card of 8.
text.scenario.b3-vs-9: Bank 3 draws against a 9. Only an 8 makes Bank 3 stand.
text.scenario.b6-vs-5: Bank 6 stands unless the Player third card is 6 or 7.
text.scenario.b6-vs-6: Bank 6 draws against a Player third card of 6 or 7.
text.inspector.OVER_DRAW: No third card is due on a natural, on Player 6 or 7, or when the Banker table says stand.
text.inspector.UNDER_DRAW: Player draws on 0 to 5; the Banker draws by its own total and the Player's third card.
text.inspector.WRONG_TOTALS_CALL: Call the Player total first, then the Banker, using the last digit of each hand.
text.inspector.WRONG_RESULT_CALL: The hand closer to 9 wins; equal totals are Égalité.
text.inspector.WRONG_COMMISSION: Banker wins pay 19 to 20: the commission is exactly 5% of the stake.
text.inspector.SHORT_PAY: Player pays 1 to 1, Banker 19 to 20, Égalité 9 to 1. Any less is a short payment.
text.inspector.OVER_PAY: Player pays 1 to 1, Banker 19 to 20, Égalité 9 to 1. Any more is an overpayment.
text.inspector.WRONG_CHANGE: Change is the chip handed over minus the 5% commission.
text.inspector.TIE_NOT_PUSHED: On Égalité, Player and Banker bets stand off: nothing paid, nothing taken.
text.inspector.COMMISSION_ON_PUNTO: Only Banker wins pay commission. Player wins are paid even money in full.
text.inspector.PAID_WRONG_SIDE: Pay only the winning hand's bets; take the losing hand's bets.
text.inspector.EGALITE_WRONG_ODDS: Égalité pays 9 to 1: a £5 bet wins £45.
